title: Reactions of Aldehydes & Ketones
page_title: Reactions of Aldehydes & Ketones | Cambridge (CIE) AS Chemistry Revision Notes 2023

blocks.md:
- **Aldehydes **and **ketones **can be reduced by reducing agents such as NaBH<sub>4</sub> or LiAlH<sub>4</sub>
- Aldehydes are reduced to **primary alcohols**
- Ketones are reduced to **secondary alcohols**

blocks.alt: Chemical reactions showing reduction of ethanal to ethanol and propanone to propan-2-ol with hydrogen, forming primary and secondary alcohols.
blocks.caption: Aldehydes are reduced to form primary alcohols, while ketones are reduced to to form secondary alcohols

blocks.md:
- Aldehydes and ketones can undergo **nucleophilic addition **with **hydrogen** **cyanide**, HCN
- The cyanide ion, CN<sup>-</sup>, acts as a nucleophile and adds across the C=O bond
- Aldehydes and ketones react with HCN, KCN as catalyst and heat to produce **hydroxynitriles**

  - Hydroxynitriles are nitriles containing a hydroxy, -OH, group

blocks.text: Nucleophilic addition of HCN to ethanal and propanone

blocks.alt: Chemical reactions showing ethanal and propanone each reacting with HCN, with KCN catalyst and heat, to form 2-hydroxypropanenitrile and 2-hydroxy-2-methylpropanenitrile.
blocks.caption: The nucleophilic addition of HCN to aldehydes other than methanal forms a chiral hydroxy nitrile compound, while the nucleophilic addition of HCN to ketones may form a chiral hydroxy nitrile compound

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md:
Catalytic hydrogenation (using H<sub>2</sub>/Pt/Ni) is indeed a powerful method that **can **reduce aldehydes and ketones to alcohols. However, this reaction often requires different (sometimes harsher) conditions than the hydrogenation of an alkene. This is not in the specification

The nucleophilic addition of HCN to an aldehyde or ketone increases the length of the carbon chain by one carbon atom!
